newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon's Bongo holds fresh Brazzaville peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's Bongo holds fresh Brazzaville peace talks.

text.p: Veteran Gabonese President Omar Bongo held separate meetings with the Congo Republic's warring parties on Tuesday amid suggestions that the two sides would soon meet face-to-face.

In the battered Congo Republic capital Brazzaville, the radio station run by former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso said envoys from the two sides would meet in Gabon's capital Libreville on Wednesday.

There was no immediate word from President Pascal Lissouba or his representatives, the opposing side in over a month of political and ethnic clashes that have killed hundreds of people, many of them civilians.
However, a fragile truce in the city was holding.
National mediators taking part in the Libreville talks said a face-to-face meeting was likely.

"We wanted to speed things up a bit and we made suggestions which have been accepted by the two sides," one said. "The aim is to continue the work but in a plenary session with the two delegations and the mediation committee."
U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, who helped Bongo end similar clashes that killed at least 2,000 people in Brazzaville in 1993, says the Congolese must discuss a solution among themselves.

The oil-producing former French colony's Constitutional Council has cancelled a planned July 27 presidential election and extended Lissouba's mandate until polling can be held. Sassou wants a government of national salvation and a parliamentary election.
The showdown began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias.
